symbols.name: ground set size
symbols.meaning: The number of elements in the ground set $[h]$, which is 100 here.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

symbols.name: set of triples
symbols.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of the ground set $[h]$.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A member of $\mathcal K$, that is, a three-element subset of $[h]$.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A member of $\mathcal K$, that is, a three-element subset of $[h]$.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, with $h=100$, and let $\mathcal K$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members $S$ and $T$ are called triples.

symbols.name: indicator vector
symbols.meaning: The 0-1 vector of length $h$ whose entries are 1 exactly at the elements of the triple $T$.
symbols.quote: For $T\in\mathcal K$, let $t_T$ be the $0$-$1$ vector of length $h$ that is $1$ exactly at the elements of $T$.

symbols.name: neighbour count
symbols.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple $T$, which is the number of triples meeting $T$ in exactly one element.
symbols.quote: For a fixed triple $T$, let $z_b$ be the number of triples meeting $T$ in exactly one element, which are the neighbours of $T$.

symbols.name: source bank
symbols.meaning: The bank of scalars with one entry $\xi_T$ per triple, which the invocation reads.
symbols.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

symbols.name: target bank
symbols.meaning: The bank of scalars with one entry $\eta_S$ per triple, which the invocation updates.
symbols.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

symbols.name: source entry
symbols.meaning: The scalar entry of the source bank $X$ indexed by the triple $T$.
symbols.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

symbols.name: target entry
symbols.meaning: The scalar entry of the target bank $Y$ indexed by the triple $S$.
symbols.quote: One invocation works on a source bank $X$ with entries $\xi_T$ and a target bank $Y$ with entries $\eta_S$, both indexed by triples.

symbols.name: side wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire carrying one scalar for each neighbour pair $(S,T)$.
symbols.quote: The invocation also has scratch wires: a side wire $W_{ST}$ for each neighbour pair $(S,T)$, and a central wire $C_\ell$ for each $\ell\in[h]$.

symbols.name: central wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire carrying one scalar for each ground element $\ell$.
symbols.quote: The invocation also has scratch wires: a side wire $W_{ST}$ for each neighbour pair $(S,T)$, and a central wire $C_\ell$ for each $\ell\in[h]$.

symbols.name: binomial coefficient
symbols.meaning: The number of $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set.
symbols.quote: The binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ counts the $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set.

relations.quote: The bit construction is a specialization of the [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md) to scalars in $\mathbb F_2$, in which two triples are neighbours when they share exactly one element.
The bit construction has its scalars in the [Binary field](binary-field.md) $\mathbb{F}_2$, where addition is exclusive or and multiplication is AND, so every scalar is a single bit.

The neighbour rule is stated in terms of the [Indicator vector](indicator-vector.md) $t_T$: for $S,T\in\mathcal K$, the intersection size is the dot product $|S\cap T| = t_S\cdot t_T$, so the rule is a condition on that dot product.
The side route is counted with the [Iverson bracket](iverson-bracket.md) $[\,|S\cap T|=1\,]$, which is $1$ when the condition holds and $0$ otherwise.
